translation.text:
<meta>The Mongolian body text on this leaf was not transcribed by the OCR because the red-ink print is faint and low in contrast. Only the Chinese side label and the archival number could be read. No content has been reconstructed.</meta>

<note>Chinese side label: "Secret Tantra, volume 11, leaf 224, front side." The original reads 秘密經第十一本上二百二十四. Chinese labels like this one helped binders and librarians keep the loose leaves of Mongolian canonical prints in order.</note>

<insert>447</insert>

<unclear>about 27 vertical lines of Mongolian (Uighur-Mongolian script) Buddhist tantric text in red ink, not transcribed</unclear>

<margin><unclear>short vertical Mongolian marginal label (volume and folio indication) at the left edge, not transcribed</unclear></margin>

<summary>This is leaf 224 of volume 11 of the Secret Tantra section of a red-ink Mongolian Buddhist canon, probably the Kanjur. The Mongolian text could not be read from the scan. Only the Chinese side label giving the section, volume and leaf number, and an archival number 447, survive in the transcription.</summary>
<keywords>Secret Tantra, Mongolian Kanjur, Buddhist tantra, Uighur-Mongolian script, red-ink print, pothi format, Chinese marginal label, volume 11, folio 224, archival number 447</keywords>
